claims.claim: Historical CCS deployment and shipping context
claims.assessment: The 2020 facility counts and project plans are not present facts or permission. Industrial-sector and projection sources remain unverified.

claims.claim: Earlier shipping studies address mode choice, liquefaction and buffers
claims.assessment: The original boundaries and comparators still need verification. The cited buffer assumptions do not establish a universal factor.

claims.claim: Waste heat supports the fixed 400 kt/year capture input
claims.assessment: Heat quantities and supplier inventories are not supplied. Voldsund’s original is not verified here.

claims.claim: Very pure CO2 allows conditioning without liquefaction loss
claims.assessment: This is an assumption needing composition and flash verification. It does not establish retention or a complete GHG boundary.

claims.claim: Expected-cost stochastic design improves investment choices
claims.assessment: This is case dependent. Expected-cost, deterministic and worst-case designs require matched objectives and scenario evidence.

claims.claim: The two-stage model forecasts entire 17-day operating seasons
claims.assessment: The authors acknowledge the optimism. An information relaxation does not quantify capacity bias or prove every component is underbuilt.

claims.claim: Thirteen scenarios represent 442 days
claims.assessment: The arithmetic is reconstructed. The scenarios are not a continuous calendar or independent operating validation.

claims.claim: Investment and recourse costs have a common annual basis
claims.assessment: The capacity conversion, scenario/season weights, annuity and construction timing remain unresolved without native arrays.

claims.claim: The receiving buffer follows physical mass conservation
claims.assessment: Equations 17–18 reverse the described inflow/outflow signs. Free cyclic inventories can admit a complementary profile, so native cost effects are not presumed.

claims.claim: Equation 21 enforces a minimum transport requirement
claims.assessment: Its printed upper bound contradicts the minimum description. The raw pooled sum also lacks displayed probability and seasonal weights.

claims.claim: Loading and unloading obey 12-hour port limits
claims.assessment: Three-hour mass variables need a rate-to-mass conversion or port time in steps. Native slots and preprocessing are unavailable.

claims.claim: Power choices adapt to weather
claims.assessment: The binary choice is indexed by scenario and season, not step. It does not specify arbitrary within-season feedback under realistic information.

claims.claim: Candidate ships have design power of 1,500–2,500 W
claims.assessment: The printed watts remain literal. A separately labelled kilowatt interpretation is only an analyst diagnostic.

claims.claim: STAwave-1 predicts sailing speed under waves
claims.assessment: Head waves, linear versus squared wave height, the undefined resistance symbol and density units require original-method verification.

claims.claim: An operator and real data validate the speed model
claims.assessment: No observations, errors, independent holdout or validation metrics are retained locally.

claims.claim: Figure 4 separates constant and increased-power cases
claims.assessment: The left panel starts near 15 knots and the right near 12, opposite the prose assignment. The curves are not independently regenerated.

claims.claim: A 25% faster strategy costs approximately 40% more fuel
claims.assessment: Hourly table ratios are 50–60%; route totals need voyage duration and weather controls. Different bases need not be contradictory.

claims.claim: The weather archive and sailing simulations characterize the route
claims.assessment: The exact MET product, interpolation and simulator are missing. Simulated histograms are not direct travel-time observations.

claims.claim: Reducing the simulations to 26 seasons preserves key properties
claims.assessment: The selection algorithm, weights, tail checks and out-of-sample objective convergence are not supplied locally.

claims.claim: Summer and winter travel-time statistics differ
claims.assessment: The printed statistics are retained. The 75% > header is ambiguous and no complete distribution is reconstructed.

claims.claim: Extreme waves occur 2.3 times per year for an average 11 hours
claims.assessment: The weather/simulation claim remains unverified and is not a ship-breakdown probability.

claims.claim: The base model solves in 435 seconds using Pyomo and Gurobi 8.1.0
claims.assessment: These are reported implementation and hardware details. Native code, logs, gap and tolerances are not reproduced.

claims.claim: The 99% case costs 143 MEUR and 33.8 EUR/t
claims.assessment: A standard annuity and transported-mass basis can match rounded values. The printed annuity and cash flows remain unresolved; this excludes capture and downstream storage costs.

claims.claim: The main cost components sum to 33.8 EUR/t
claims.assessment: The four-component sum is reconstructed. Some finer graph and energy sums can differ within rounding intervals, without proving a typo.

claims.claim: Conditioning electricity costs 7.8 EUR/t
claims.assessment: Dividing cost by price is a conditional component estimate, not a complete process or utility/supplier inventory.

claims.claim: The 99% and 100% cases require different source buffers
claims.assessment: 5,120 t is 102.4% of ship mass; 5,890 t is 117.8%. Fractions of cycle emissions use another denominator and the cases must remain distinct.

claims.claim: Summer slowing saves 1 MEUR or 0.24 EUR/t
claims.assessment: The reported policy is not reproduced. Only the discounted arithmetic and rounding can be checked.

claims.claim: The last percentage point costs 41.9 EUR/t with a 24% premium
claims.assessment: Rounded incremental cost can support this statement under a disclosed annuity comparison. It is not capture or retention performance.

claims.claim: Extra buffers can recover a 12-hour delay or longer disruption
claims.assessment: Recovery depends on slack, inventory boundaries and valid extreme-weather modelling. It is not guaranteed service availability.

claims.claim: Ignoring weather at design causes a 6.4 MEUR loss
claims.assessment: A native VSS comparison needs matched information, probabilities, objectives and service. The reported design is not independently rerun.

claims.claim: Ignoring delays raises cost by 1.9 EUR/t and venting by 4,000 t/year
claims.assessment: The body includes fuel, penalties and capital effects, while the conclusion calls the increase fuel cost. Different transported-mass bases may explain part of the arithmetic, but remain unverified.

claims.claim: The deterministic design uses 25% more fuel and powers up in 53% of scenarios
claims.assessment: These are reported conditional policy results, not a universal penalty for deterministic planning.

claims.claim: At 10% seasonal variation, the 5,000 t ship remains preferable
claims.assessment: The 1.3 EUR/t margin, 3,250 t venting and buffer changes require native season weights and schedules.

claims.claim: At 20–30% variation, the 7,500 t ship is preferable
claims.assessment: The full comparison is not reproduced. The reported 5,445 t cycle exceeds the smaller ship by 445 t.

claims.claim: Seasonal storage is never cost-effective
claims.assessment: Separate cyclic seasons forbid storage between months. The general claim requires a feasible comparison that permits that strategy.

claims.claim: Higher fuel prices increase the value of buffers
claims.assessment: This is deterministic sensitivity rather than a calibrated joint fuel-price uncertainty model. The final percentage label also needs reconciliation.

claims.claim: Underinvestment is more costly than overinvestment
claims.assessment: The reported 2.1 versus 0.73 MEUR losses concern particular cross-evaluated price/design cases, not a general theorem.

claims.claim: One annual ship breakdown can justify an 8,660 t buffer
claims.assessment: The case assumes no concurrent weather disruption and lacks an empirical fault law. Native inventory and cost timing remain unavailable.

claims.claim: Added breakdown storage is 2,760 t and totals 173% of ship capacity
claims.assessment: The displayed endpoint difference is 2,770 t; rounding or version differences may matter. The total ratio is 173.2%, not an annual-service factor.

claims.claim: The 118% buffer is the base optimum at the lowest reported unit cost
claims.assessment: The 118% ship ratio belongs to the 100% case. The 99% case with 33.8 EUR/t has a 102.4% source-buffer ratio.

claims.claim: Fuel and breakdown findings transfer to other chains
claims.assessment: The cost, weather and schedule assumptions are case specific. No regional injection or complete GHG factor follows.

claims.claim: iCCS, HYSYS and APEA supply the process and cost functions
claims.assessment: Native files, factors and fitted coefficients are not retained. The one original-source check supports method context under a different offshore boundary.

claims.claim: All costs are updated to 2017 prices
claims.assessment: Exact index values, dates, currencies and regional adjustments are not available for each component.

claims.claim: Conditioning produces liquid CO2 at 6.5 bar and minus 50 C
claims.assessment: Pressure basis, composition, EOS and complete stream duties remain missing. The PFD is not a complete inventory.

claims.claim: Fixed O&M equals 5.5% of capital
claims.assessment: Rounded conditioning and buffer values agree. The reconditioning coefficient does not agree on the same printed basis.

claims.claim: Buffer investment costs 1,130 EUR/m3
claims.assessment: The implied mass-density conversion is not an EOS validation. The unqualified Roussanaly 2013 attribution remains ambiguous.

claims.claim: Harbor costs scale from 7.9 MEUR at 3 Mt/year
claims.assessment: The prose exponent is 0.85 and the displayed appendix exponent is 0.8. Neither is silently selected as the correction.

claims.claim: Ship capital and fixed operating costs have a consistent version
claims.assessment: The 5,000 t investment and O&M values differ among Tables 1, 2 and 6. Their scope and version need native reconciliation.

claims.claim: Utility prices define operating cost inputs
claims.assessment: Prices alone do not establish quantities, supplier emissions or complete capture-chain burdens.

claims.claim: The KPI uses 25 years, 8% and a 40/30/30 construction schedule
claims.assessment: The actual cash-flow dates must agree with the objective and annuity. The named Anantharaman authority has no complete bibliography entry.

claims.claim: The supplementary data enables reproduction
claims.assessment: Appendix B gives a DOI, but the external asset is not retained. Public contents, versions and rights are unverified under the Chrome pause.

claims.claim: The bibliography identifies supporting originals
claims.assessment: All 44 entries are retained, including the Jakobsen duplicate candidate. One scoped check does not verify the other 43 entries or twelve dependencies.
